Row (a) cannot be reached on this record, and neither can the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e), because the deviation is 1.80 km.

The driver's in-app message asserting a closure cannot supply the traffic justification the matrix depends on. claims.text: The driver told the rider he was leaving the recommended route before he left it, and the rider agreed. MSG-05020-003 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?') was sent at 18:41:22 and read at 18:41:33, and the rider answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47; the platform's own deviation event is timed at 18:44:22 at Bukit Timah Road / Farrer Road, three minutes later. POL-RD-21's obligation to inform the rider by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation is therefore met on the chat log, and where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the clause treats the deviation as agreed. The rider does not deny the exchange; she says only that she agreed on the strength of what the driver told her.

The record's only traffic data points at the very segment the driver left and names the very road he took. EV-ADVIS-05020-01 is a ROAD_CLOSURE on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road with the message 'Diversion via Holland Rd'; the driver's deviation point was Bukit Timah Road / Farrer Road at 18:44:22, and the trace places him on Holland Road from 18:44:30 and on Napier Road thereafter (the rejoin at Kim Seng Road / Tanglin Road at 18:57:37). He did not improvise a shortcut: he took the road the traffic authority designates for that closed segment. I put this honestly and do not overstate POL-RD-23: the advisory's stated validity window (00:30-05:30) does not overlap the trip window, so I do not contend that the window limb of POL-RD-23 is satisfied on this artifact. The point is narrower and it stands: the driver's account of a closure on that stretch is corroborated by the authority's own record for that road on that day, whereas the rider's assertion that the road was 'open and moving' is a bare statement with no traffic data of any kind behind it.

The rider's change of mind does not undo her recorded agreement. POL-RD-21 makes the deviation 'agreed' where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and it does; POL-RD-24's rows turn on whether the reroute was traffic-justified, whether the rider was informed and the size of the deviation - the driver's motive in choosing the route is not an element of any row, and 'she agreed only because he said it was closed' is a complaint about the premise of the driver's message, not a denial that he disclosed the reroute and she accepted it. A reroute the driver announced in writing, that the rider answered in writing, and that delivered her to Great World as booked, cannot be re-characterised hours later as an unauthorised detour.

On the driver's case the 1.30 SGD must come back to him as DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and on any view of POL-RD-24 nothing further may be taken from him. POL-RD-24 measures the excess distance fare as deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd with no surge: 1.80 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.296, rounded to 1.30 SGD. That is exactly the sum the platform has already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (fare_adjusted at 20:14:30; payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 1.30). The recovery is therefore already at the ceiling POL-RD-24 permits, and if the judge accepts the driver's primary case the whole of that 1.30 SGD is what the driver is owed under POL-GEN-03's DRIVER_COMPENSATION.

If the judge is not with the driver on the primary case, the driver asks in the alternative for ESCALATE under POL-RD-24's own escalation limb read with POL-GEN-26. What the parties actually dispute is the effect of the rider's 'ok sure': she was informed of the deviation and she now objects, saying her agreement was given only because the driver said the road was closed. That is the consent configuration the limb reserves for human review ('informed but the rider objected') because the refund rows do not answer it, and the question whether the rider's agreement holds is a fact the rows cannot settle. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated fee is held rather than finally paid over while a reviewer decides, so escalation preserves the 1.30 SGD pending that review instead of finally putting it beyond the driver's reach.

ruling.explanation:
Driver D-59361 filed this dispute asking for the 1.30 SGD already refunded to rider R-78242 and recovered from the driver's earnings. The driver's claim fails, and the present state stands.

How I get there. The deviation is fixed by POL-RD-22 at the platform's recorded distances: 11.6 km actual minus 9.8 km optimal = 1.80 km (EV-TRIP-05020), which is above the 1.0 km tolerance. The only traffic data in the record, EV-ADVIS-05020-01, is a road closure on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road, but it is valid 00:30-05:30 on 14 September while the trip ran 18:34:30-19:00:30 the same day. The advisory does not overlap the trip window, so POL-RD-23's traffic-justification test is not met; a driver's own assertion of a closure, with no qualifying data, does not justify the reroute. Because the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeded 1 km, row (d) of POL-RD-24 governs and the excess distance fare is refunded in full: 1.80 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.296, rounded to 1.30 SGD (EV-FARE-05020). That is exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (refund_issued_sgd 1.30; payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED; fare_adjusted at 20:14:30).

On the driver's arguments. I accept that the driver told the rider in writing before deviating: MSG-05020-003 at 18:41:22 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?'), read 18:41:33, answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, with the platform's deviation event at 18:44:22 (EV-CHAT-05020, EV-TRIP-05020). POL-RD-21's notice limb is met and the rider's acknowledgment is on the log. But that agreement only matters in row (a) of POL-RD-24, which also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, and that condition is absent, so it is outweighed. The driver's reading of the advisory is also rejected: the right road is named, but the record's effective window is thirteen hours before the trip, and the driver himself does not contend the window limb is satisfied. The rider's change of mind is therefore beside the point -- where the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, row (d) refunds the excess distance fare regardless of what the rider agreed to at the time.

On the driver's alternative request for escalation. POL-RD-24 escalates only a case that fits no row, such as 'informed but the rider objected'. This case fits row (d) squarely, so it is not such a case and I do not escalate. No fact needed by the matrix is missing or impaired: every artifact I relied on is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-GEN-26 has no work to do.

The rider's points are accepted: the deviation 1.80 km is over tolerance, the reroute is not traffic-justified, row (d) applies, and the row (d) remedy is the 1.30 SGD already with the rider. The amount contested is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final here at a confidence at or above POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar.

Outcome for the party who filed: the driver filed, the rider is owed the 1.30 SGD already refunded, so the driver's claim fails and the present state stands -- NO_ACTION, with both amounts null. No referral clause applies to a route deviation in this version.

Both parties filed here: the driver contests the 1.30 SGD the platform has already refunded to the rider and recovered from him. On this policy the rider is owed that sum, so the driver's claim fails and the present state stands — NO_ACTION, with both money amounts null.

What the record shows. The recommended route was 9.8 km and the route actually driven was 11.6 km (trip record EV-TRIP-05020), a deviation of 1.80 km. POL-RD-22 fixes the measurement on those recorded distances and sets the tolerance at 1.0 km, so this is not a within-tolerance case; the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05020) is not used to re-measure the distance.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The only traffic data in the record, the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05020-01, is a road closure on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road valid 00:30–05:30 on 14 September. The trip ran 18:34:30–19:00:30 that day, roughly thirteen hours after that window closed; the artifact's own finding is overlaps_trip_window = false and justifies_reroute = false. POL-RD-23 requires the data to intersect the recommended route and overlap the trip window, and it says a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The driver's in-app message MSG-05020-003 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?') is exactly such an assertion. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified.

Refund matrix (POL-RD-24). With the reroute not traffic-justified and the deviation over 1 km, row (d) governs: the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That is 1.80 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.296, rounded to 1.30 SGD, with no surge. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-05020) records refund_issued_sgd 1.30 and payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, and the trip record's fare_adjusted event (20:14:30) shows the 1.30 SGD was refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

On the driver's notification and the rider's reply. The driver did tell the rider before he left the route — MSG-05020-003 at 18:41:22, the rider's 'ok sure' at 18:41:47, the platform's deviation event at 18:44:22 — so POL-RD-21's notification limb is met on the chat log and the acknowledgment is recorded. But that does not reach row (a), which is the only no-refund row and which additionally requires the reroute to be traffic-justified; it is not. Where the reroute is not traffic-justified, rows (d) and (e) turn on the size of the deviation alone, so the agreement does not remove the refund the rider is owed.

On the driver's alternative request for escalation under POL-RD-24 read with POL-GEN-26: it does not apply. The escalated example in POL-RD-24 — 'informed but the rider objected' — is a traffic-justified case that fits neither row (a) (no agreement) nor row (b) (rider informed), and so fits no row. Here the reroute is not traffic-justified, so the case fits row (d) squarely. POL-GEN-26 is not engaged either: the deviation distance and the traffic position are both established on complete artifacts (all weight 1.0), so there is no fact the record cannot carry.

Decision and confidence. The amount contested is 1.30 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, and the POL-RD-25 confidence bar of 0.80 is met; the deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05020, EV-ADVIS-05020-01, EV-FARE-05020), so confidence is set at 0.90. A route deviation produces no referral clause in this version, so none is made.

The trip ran 18:34:30 to 19:00:30, so the advisory's window closed about thirteen hours before the journey; its own derived finding records overlaps_trip_window = false and justifies_reroute = false. ledger.claim: The deviation here is 1.80 km and it is not within tolerance. POL-RD-22 fixes the measurement at the platform's recorded distances — trip_record.actual_distance_km 11.6 km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km 9.8 km = 1.80 km — and says in terms that the GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the trace's 9.795 km figure is therefore not the measure. The tolerance under POL-RD-22 is 1.0 km, so 1.80 km puts this case squarely in the over-1-km half of the POL-RD-24 matrix, on complete evidence at weight 1.0.

The reroute has no traffic justification on this record. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data intersects the recommended route segment and overlaps the trip window. The single advisory filed, LTA-TI-260914-6951 (EV-ADVIS-05020-01), is a ROAD_CLOSURE on Bukit Timah Road between Farrer Road and Cluny Road valid from 2026-09-14 00:30 to 05:30; the trip ran 18:34:30 to 19:00:30 the same day, some thirteen hours after the closure window closed. Row (d) of POL-RD-24 therefore governs: the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The row the driver needs, row (a) — no refund because the reroute was traffic-justified and the rider was informed and agreed — additionally requires traffic justification, and that condition is absent. Row (a) cannot be reached on this record, and neither can the within-tolerance rows (c) and (e), because the deviation is 1.80 km.

The row (d) remedy is precisely the sum already with the rider. The excess distance fare is 1.80 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.296, rounded to 1.30, with no surge applied, and the fare ledger records refund_issued_sgd 1.30 with payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED and the trip record's fare_adjusted event shows that 1.30 was refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver. The driver's claim for that 1.30 back is not supported, so under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is NO_ACTION — the present state stands — and because the filer is the driver, NO_ACTION leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

The driver's in-app message asserting a closure cannot supply the traffic justification the matrix depends on. POL-RD-23 states that a driver's assertion of traffic with no qualifying data does not justify the reroute, and MSG-05020-003 ("Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?") is the only place that closure claim appears — the filing carries no advisory covering the trip window. The rider's account at filing is to the same effect: the road was open and moving, and she agreed only because the driver told her it was closed.

The rider's reply "ok sure" does not turn this into an agreed, no-refund reroute. POL-RD-21's acknowledgment limb feeds row (a) of POL-RD-24, and row (a) still requires traffic justification, which this record lacks; the acknowledgment was given in direct response to the driver's closure assertion, which the advisory data does not bear out at 18:44. Whether the driver's notice was timely is not outcome-determinative in any event, because rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both refund the same excess distance fare, and only row (a) avoids a refund — and row (a) is out of reach.

Nothing here requires escalation under POL-GEN-26, because every fact the matrix needs is established. The recorded distances, the notification, the traffic data and the fare and refund are each carried by a COMPLETE artifact at weight 1.0, and each of those artifacts' pre-pass notes records an empty issue list, so no deciding fact is carried by missing or impaired evidence.

The amount the driver asks back is 1.30 SGD — dispute.amount_contested_sgd, the same 1.30 the ledger shows refunded — which is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold. The AI ruling is therefore final at any confidence on this dispute, and the case is to be decided rather than escalated.

The driver told the rider he was leaving the recommended route before he left it, and the rider agreed. MSG-05020-003 ('Bukit Timah Road got road closure, I go Holland Road ok?') was sent at 18:41:22 and read at 18:41:33, and the rider answered 'ok sure' at 18:41:47; the platform's own deviation event is timed at 18:44:22 at Bukit Timah Road / Farrer Road, three minutes later. POL-RD-21's obligation to inform the rider by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation is therefore met on the chat log, and where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the clause treats the deviation as agreed. The rider does not deny the exchange; she says only that she agreed on the strength of what the driver told her.

The record's only traffic data points at the very segment the driver left and names the very road he took. EV-ADVIS-05020-01 is a ROAD_CLOSURE on Bukit Timah Road (towards City) between Farrer Road and Cluny Road with the message 'Diversion via Holland Rd'; the driver's deviation point was Bukit Timah Road / Farrer Road at 18:44:22, and the trace places him on Holland Road from 18:44:30 and on Napier Road thereafter (the rejoin at Kim Seng Road / Tanglin Road at 18:57:37). He did not improvise a shortcut: he took the road the traffic authority designates for that closed segment. I put this honestly and do not overstate POL-RD-23: the advisory's stated validity window (00:30-05:30) does not overlap the trip window, so I do not contend that the window limb of POL-RD-23 is satisfied on this artifact. The point is narrower and it stands: the driver's account of a closure on that stretch is corroborated by the authority's own record for that road on that day, whereas the rider's assertion that the road was 'open and moving' is a bare statement with no traffic data of any kind behind it.

The rider's change of mind does not undo her recorded agreement. POL-RD-21 makes the deviation 'agreed' where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and it does; POL-RD-24's rows turn on whether the reroute was traffic-justified, whether the rider was informed and the size of the deviation - the driver's motive in choosing the route is not an element of any row, and 'she agreed only because he said it was closed' is a complaint about the premise of the driver's message, not a denial that he disclosed the reroute and she accepted it. A reroute the driver announced in writing, that the rider answered in writing, and that delivered her to Great World as booked, cannot be re-characterised hours later as an unauthorised detour.

On the driver's case the 1.30 SGD must come back to him as DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and on any view of POL-RD-24 nothing further may be taken from him. POL-RD-24 measures the excess distance fare as deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd with no surge: 1.80 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.296, rounded to 1.30 SGD. That is exactly the sum the platform has already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver (fare_adjusted at 20:14:30; payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 1.30). The recovery is therefore already at the ceiling POL-RD-24 permits, and if the judge accepts the driver's primary case the whole of that 1.30 SGD is what the driver is owed under POL-GEN-03's DRIVER_COMPENSATION.

If the judge is not with the driver on the primary case, the driver asks in the alternative for ESCALATE under POL-RD-24's own escalation limb read with POL-GEN-26. What the parties actually dispute is the effect of the rider's 'ok sure': she was informed of the deviation and she now objects, saying her agreement was given only because the driver said the road was closed. That is the consent configuration the limb reserves for human review ('informed but the rider objected') because the refund rows do not answer it, and the question whether the rider's agreement holds is a fact the rows cannot settle. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated fee is held rather than finally paid over while a reviewer decides, so escalation preserves the 1.30 SGD pending that review instead of finally putting it beyond the driver's reach.
